mentions.name: A5
mentions.description: A5 is a pentagonal geospatial index with semantics familiar to H3 users, whose cells have exactly the same area globally. It ships implementations in TypeScript, Python, and Rust, and has a growing ecosystem of community ports and integrations, including DuckDB and QGIS.
mentions.source_excerpt:
A5 - a pentagonal geospatial index: https://a5geo.org

If you’ve used H3 the semantics should be familiar. The biggest differentiator is the fact that cells have exactly the same area globally, for why this matters see: https://a5geo.org/docs/recipes/a5-vs-h3

mentions.name: A5
mentions.description: An open-source pentagonal geospatial indexing system. Familiar to users of H3 or S2, but built on pentagons with practically uniform cell areas, whereas alternative systems have a variance of around 2 between their largest and smallest cells, making them less useful for aggregation. The project website includes visual demos.
mentions.problem: Alternative geospatial indexing systems such as H3 and S2 have a variance of around 2 between their largest and smallest cell areas, making them less useful for aggregation.
mentions.source_excerpt:
A pentagonal geospatial indexing system: https://a5geo.org/

If you’ve used H3 or S2 it should be familiar, the major difference (apart from the fact it uses pentagons) is that the cell areas are practically uniform, whereas alternative systems have a variance of around 2 between the largest and smallest cells, making them less useful for aggregation. The site has many visual demos, e.g. https://a5geo.org/examples/area

The code is open source: https://github.com/felixpalmer/a5
